prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The map shows a mostly open campsite with the ground nearest the camera bright and the cliff and sky farthest away dark; a person remains roughly 2–4 m in front while the picnic table, chairs, coolers, and supplies cluster at about 2–6 m, and the truck sits farther left or right at roughly 5–10 m depending on the frame. Across the five frames, the camera wearer approaches the person and table: the person grows from a narrow mid-distance figure to a large near-field shape, reaching approximately 1–2 m away in the last two frames, while the table objects also become nearer and more partly occluded by the person. The person is first centered and facing mostly away, then shifts toward the right side of the view as the camera turns or passes left of them; the depth map supports front-to-back ordering and reveals that the nearby person is in front of the table and chairs more clearly than RGB alone. Large smooth gradients and halos around silhouettes, merged depths among adjacent table objects, the nearly black cliff/sky, and bright foreground rocks indicate unreliable metric scale and weak boundaries, so all metre estimates are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates one person, the truck, and campsite objects including chairs, a bench, backpacks, an umbrella, and later a suitcase, showing which overlapping RGB regions belong to separate instances. In the first frames the person is about 2–4 m ahead near the table, with chairs and bags roughly 1–3 m from that person and the truck several metres farther to the right; later the person occupies the center-right foreground at about 1–2 m, partly blocking the table and nearby objects, while the truck appears on the left and then at the far right edge as the view rotates. The masks show left/right layout and occlusion especially well: small chairs and bags lie left of or behind the person, the bench is to the person's right in one middle frame, and the truck is repeatedly clipped by the image boundary. The map is unreliable for distance and vertical ordering because it contains no direct depth, misses much of the terrain and many table items, changes labels for small similar objects, and sometimes produces incomplete or coarse masks; it also cannot establish gaze direction beyond the rough orientation visible from the person's silhouette.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects one person's body in the middle three frames and a partial upper-body or arm configuration in the last frame, making limb configuration and body orientation clearer than in RGB despite background clutter. The person is roughly 2–3 m ahead in the third frame, mostly facing away, then about 1–2 m ahead and turned partly sideways in the fourth; in the fifth, only a sparse head-and-arm skeleton remains near the right side as the person is very close, partly occluded, and partly outside the reliable pose field. The skeleton suggests the arms are close to the torso at first and later extend toward objects on the table, which are within that person's arm's reach, while nothing shown establishes that the person looks directly at the camera wearer. The map gives almost no scene layout, object distance, or camera-wearer's hand reach on its own, misses the person entirely in the first two frames, shows no magenta hand detections, and becomes anatomically incomplete or distorted under turning, proximity, occlusion, and cropping.
